name: Limbe Botanic Garden & Black Sand Beach
description: A lush botanical garden founded in 1892 sitting right above Limbe's volcanic black-sand coastline, with views of Mount Cameroon rising behind the Atlantic.

name: Mount Cameroon
description: West Africa's tallest peak and an active volcano, offering a multi-day trek through rainforest, savanna, and volcanic scree to a 4,040m summit.

name: Waza National Park
description: A UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in the Sahelian north, home to elephants, giraffes, lions, and hundreds of bird species across open savanna.

name: Rhumsiki (Mandara Mountains)
description: A village in the volcanic Mandara Mountains famous for its dramatic rock spires, Kapsiki culture, and traditional crab-divination ceremonies.

name: Foumban Royal Palace & Museum
description: Seat of the Bamoun Kingdom since the 14th century, with a royal museum housing masks, thrones, and artifacts spanning centuries of Bamoun history.

name: Kribi Beach & Lobe Waterfalls
description: White-sand Atlantic beaches meet the rare sight of the Lobe Falls cascading directly into the ocean, just south of Kribi town.

name: Dja Faunal Reserve
description: A UNESCO World Heritage rainforest reserve, one of the largest and best-protected in Africa, home to gorillas, chimpanzees, and forest elephants.

name: Yaoundé — Seven Hills Capital
description: Cameroon's hilltop capital, blending government architecture, the National Museum, vibrant markets, and a growing food and nightlife scene.

name: Douala — Economic Capital
description: Cameroon's largest city and main port, known for its energetic street food scene, art galleries, and the lively Akwa nightlife district.

name: Bafut Palace
description: The traditional seat of the Fon of Bafut, a UNESCO-tentative-list palace complex of carved wooden buildings reflecting Grassfields kingdom heritage.
